page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine optimized for lower memory ratios and local storage needs. Powered by a 3.4 GHz ARM Neoverse-N2 processor, it features 16 dedicated physical cores (1 thread per core) delivering 16 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 128 MB L3 cache, and 944 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage. The instance operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and lacks discrete GPU acceleration or x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX.

Benchmark evaluations reveal balanced compute metrics and superior memory subsystem performance. The ARM core architecture posted average results across stress-ng single-core (2,074.98) and multi-core (33,160.55), Geekbench multi-core (14,736.0), and PassMark CPU (14,693.2). However, large-block memory throughput reaches the top 25%, delivering 307.54 GB/sec for read operations and 124.58 GB/sec for write operations, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 2,945.61. Compression throughput is also strong, achieving 33.08 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip tests.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio marks a deliberate tradeoff between compute density and memory capacity. While large models struggle—such as medium 7B LLM prompt processing lagging in the bottom 25% at 24.62 tokens/sec—the instance delivers strong throughput on smaller language tasks, reaching 263.31 tokens/sec for 135M model generation. Paired with 944 GB of low-latency NVMe SSD storage and solid static web serving throughput (27.37 GB/sec), the D16plds_v6 provides high resource density per core for I/O-heavy caching tiers, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and web frontends that do not require expansive memory allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose instance configured with 16 dedicated Neoverse-N2 cores operating at 3.4 GHz, 32.0 GB of RAM, and 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking discrete GPUs, it features a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation suited for compute-focused and disk-reliant workloads. Benchmarks demonstrate solid overall compute with average scores in Geekbench (14,736.0 multi-core) and PassMark CPU (14,693.2), coupled with strong memory bandwidth reaching 307.54 GB/sec on uncached reads. While limited RAM restricts broader database or large-scale AI applications, its fast local NVMe storage and strong small-model throughput make it an efficient option for CI/CD runners, build servers, static web hosting, and distributed caching services.
